gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the $359.99 Grandfalls Plus delivers the same rated cleaning output as the Active 2.3 (2,100 PSI × 1.2 GPM = 2,520 CU vs 1,100 PSI × 2.3 GPM = 2,530 CU), which works out to $0.14 per cleaning unit against $0.51 for Active's own 100 ft wall-mount kit. The Active's real edge is 1.9× the water flow, not more total output.
standout_why: I compared against totimes.ca, progaragegear.com and bobvila.com, all opened today, plus ChatGPT's own answers. totimes.ca lists rated PSI and GPM side by side for the Pro, Plus and Active 2.3 and says 'Compare rated PSI and rated GPM together', but it never multiplies them and never divides by price. progaragegear.com gives only maximum figures and the horsepower formula (PSI×GPM/1,714), with no rated cleaning units and no cost per unit. bobvila.com states only 3,700 PSI and 100 ft and gives no GPM. ChatGPT pitched the Active 2.3 as the 'higher-performance' pick at about $700–$1,100. None of these pages show that its total rated output equals the Plus, or that Active's own wall-mount kits cost $1,187–$1,292.
decides: This supports the Grandfalls Plus as the value pick. At rated output it matches the Active 2.3 for about 28% of the price of Active's 100 ft wall-mount kit, and its 100 ft auto-retract reel is built in. The Grandfalls Pro delivers the most rated output for the money among the all-in-ones I could source (3,240 CU, $0.18/CU), so it stays the all-in-one pick. The Active 2.3 is worth it only if the buyer mainly wants water volume for rinsing cars and running a foam cannon: 2.3 vs 1.2 GPM is 1.9× the water. It is not worth it for driveway or patio cleaning power. ChatGPT's $700–$1,100 budget for an Active setup is too low next to Active's own wall-mount kits.
